1._: A RUNG — one knot on the stack. Depth is order: the deepest rung tied is where the work is, and the first untied is what comes next. Each rung is the address where one act stands, in its own mind's block, and nothing is copied onto the thread. The proposal: the rung also carries the addresses its act read, beside it, so the next mind loads the context the last one used; when and who come from the beach's stamp and the writer's key.

1.4: THE SEAT, CLOSEST ALREADY — a session that walks through the play door holds a seat in the router: the beach it stands at, the hand, the bundle its shell dialed, and the stamp of its last ack; on every ack after, the router compiles the bundle against that stamp and says only what moved (src/orientation.ts, 11 October). It lives in the router's memory, ends with the session, and belongs to one hand. A thread is that seat kept on the beach as rungs, so a second mind, in any harness and at any later time, takes the work up and is told what moved since.
1.5: WHY THE KEEPER FAILED — the trial's keeper held the spine's lock and tied every rung (spine:beacon, weft). By the beach's own law that is a central resolver (strata 4.1: meaning scales because there is no central resolver anywhere in the design); the rungs are unbounded state, which any mind appends with no race (strata 3.4); and a law with no loop sits inert until its one hand is sent (strata 3.3). Matthew's golden flow names the same slide: protocols and rules that keep growing pull a system toward the organised corner (spine:golden-flow 1.94). In the trial two of the four rungs restate a mirror's line at the self-same address, and the second mind's brief named the rung it should write (watch:weft 682.9, 686). A keeper is what a thread becomes when it has memory and nothing to wake the next mind.
